## 油價下跌，美債仍因實質殖利率上升而走弱

週一美國債市在六月節假期後恢復交易。美伊協議取得進展、油價下跌，美債卻沿著曲線全面走弱。2年期殖利率上升5個基點至4.24%，10年期也上升5個基點至4.51%；5年期上升6個基點至4.29%，30年期上升5個基點至4.95%。10年期實質殖利率升幅比名目殖利率還大，通膨補償反而下降。投資人要求更高的實質報酬，並未因油價回落而提高長期通膨溢價。

芝加哥Fed總裁Austan Goolsbee指出，服務通膨正朝錯誤方向發展，難以單用關稅或伊朗衝突推升能源價格來解釋。紐約Fed一項研究模型，也上修通膨、成長與均衡實質利率估計。這些看法接續Kevin Warsh首次主持的會議；當時官員提高通膨預測，交易員開始反映10月前升息。光靠油價下跌，已不足以讓美債殖利率同步回落。

融資與股市消息讓這個對比更鮮明。SpaceX開始就至少$200億投資級債券與投資人接觸，股價卻下跌16%。Sony也重返美元債市場，兩筆大額國庫券標售則順利找到買盤，顯示資金仍可取得，只是代價提高。英國首相更替後，英國公債稍獲喘息；加拿大通膨擴散，則帶來相反的政策壓力。新興市場方面，哥倫比亞大選結果推升公債與貨幣，巴西卻取消通膨連動債標售，並介入外匯市場。

## 政策風險推高實質殖利率

2年與10年期美債利差維持27個基點，2年與30年期維持71個基點；一週以來，兩者分別收窄13及19個基點。5年期略為落後兩側天期，使2s5s10s蝶式利差上升2個基點至−17個基點，2s10s30s維持−17個基點。週一債價再次下跌，但長端沒有重新帶頭陡峭化。

5年期實質殖利率上升5個基點至2.01%，7年期上升6個基點至2.13%，10年期上升7個基點至2.28%；20及30年期則分別上升6與5個基點，至2.58%及2.75%。10年期損益兩平通膨率下降2個基點至2.23%，實質殖利率上升的幅度超過其影響。這種背離，延續了六月節休市前Fed帶來的利率調整。

Goolsbee特別擔憂服務通膨，認為無法輕易歸因於暫時的能源或關稅因素。他也願意減少預先給出的利率指引，與Warsh希望讓政策更依當期數據調整的方向一致。紐約Fed 6月DSGE研究模型將2026年核心PCE預測從3月的2.5%上修至3.1%，GDP成長由1.0%上修至1.2%，第4季自然實質利率估計由1.9%升至2.0%。這些是研究模型的結果，並非Fed正式政策預測；但通膨、成長與均衡實質利率同步上修，為實質殖利率維持偏高提供了具體理由。

短券顯示，眼前資金環境與未來政策利率預期並不相同。4及6週國庫券殖利率分別下降3及1個基點至3.63%與3.65%，13週收在3.79%，52週為4.03%。愈往後段、殖利率愈高，較符合預期Fed維持緊縮，而非最短天期資金普遍突然短缺。

財政部標售$890億91天期國庫券，最高得標貼現利率3.695%，換算投資利率3.782%，投標倍數2.68。在$871.68億競爭性得標金額中，間接投標人獲配$520.87億、直接投標人$42.38億、交易商$308.43億。另筆$770億182天期國庫券，得標貼現利率3.840%、投資利率3.970%，投標倍數2.51，最高得標利率的配售比例為97.87%；在$755.53億競爭性得標金額中，間接、直接投標人與交易商分別獲配$400.73億、$30.00億及$324.81億。兩筆均於6月25日交割。大量國庫券仍取得認購，交割所需資金則要到本週稍晚才會移轉。

## SpaceX股價下跌，首筆發債方案逐漸成形

SpaceX開始為首筆投資級美元債接觸投資人，目標規模至少$200億，天期橫跨5年至30年。資金預計用於再融資規模相近的過橋貸款，該貸款占公司$291億長期債務的大部分。穆迪給予Baa1、惠譽BBB+、S&P給予BBB評級；公司表示，截至6月19日現金及約當現金接近$1,010億。債券尚未完成定價，也沒有最終訂單簿。

SpaceX股價當天下跌16%至$154.60，3個交易日累計下跌23%，市值蒸發逾$6,000億。儘管如此，股價仍比$135 IPO價格高約15%；上市首日可交易股份只占總股數4.2%，低流通量放大了波動。正在籌備的發債，則讓市場開始衡量龐大資本支出對現金的需求。一項分析師預測，SpaceX淨負債可能由近期約$130億升至2031年逾$4,000億；這是未來情境，不是目前資產負債表上的數字。

6月中旬以前，投資級債券發行已超過$1,200億，上半年發行速度高出常態3個標準差。最大15筆交易占約57%，包括輝達約$250億發債；在這波供給下，信用利差變動仍不大。但發行集中於少數大型科技業者，後續供給將檢驗買方是否繼續接受相同條件。自去年11月以來，科技企業已在各類信用市場籌得逾$3,000億AI相關債務；輝達前次訂單超過發行額3倍。

Sony也加入日本高評級美元債發行隊列，開始為5及10年期、用於一般企業用途的債券與投資人接觸。這將是自1998年發行$15億以來，首次重返美國美元債市場；預期評級為A2及A+。Denso的$5億美元債、三菱的$10億交易及Toyota的€10億發行，同樣顯示日本企業在本地利率上升時分散融資管道。

Robinhood則尋求減少現金利息支出，推介$20億、2029年到期的零息可轉債，轉換溢價區間為60%至65%。約$3億擬用於股票回購，另有衍生性工具安排，目標是在相對參考股價上漲125%的範圍內抵銷股權稀釋。定價預定在紐約收盤後進行；當日可見的是推介條件與資金用途，尚非已完成發行。

印度證券化市場也提供銀行另一條融資路徑。截至3月的年度，資產擔保證券發行達1.53兆盧比，外國銀行比重由前兩個會計年度的28%至30%，升至約35%。零售貸款池可滿足優先領域放款要求，部分交易所需監理資本也低於直接貸款。Aye Finance表示，貸款證券化成本比本地公司債低75至100個基點，因為貸款池評級比公司本身高3至4級。這項節省仍取決於零售、車貸、個人及黃金貸款的實際表現。

較脆弱的借款人，必須協商的不只是殖利率。Godiva Japan正向25家銀行尋求將月底到期、約¥750億、約合$4.64億債務展延9個月；若公司違約，三菱UFJ正考慮提供清償順位高於舊債的¥50億新資金。Godiva在2025年虧損約¥300億，權益比率降至約7%，一般日本企業則約40%或更高。展延可以換取時間，新的優先順位融資卻可能改變現有債權人的回收位置。

德意志銀行分析師認為，Paragon的€4.5億、2030年到期有擔保債，合理價格為面額每€1的€0.70至€0.75，低於市價約€0.83，理由是併購帶動槓桿與整合風險。公司則強調客戶留存穩定、前10大客戶只占淨營收約27%，且2030年前沒有重大到期壓力。爭議在於未來信用品質，而非眼前付款困難。英國一套涵蓋交易場所逾95%債券的整合交易資訊系統，也已上線，讓市場更容易觀察次級市場價格。

加州可能增加公共債券供給。州議員同意把$113億住宅方案交付11月選民表決，其中包含$100億一般責任債及$12.5億以自身收入償付的退伍軍人房貸債；另有$120億科學與醫療提案仍在討論。這些債券尚未獲選民通過，也未發行。方案因應獨棟住宅房價中位數高於$90萬的問題，若獲授權，也會增加公共長天期債券供給。

信用ETF隨美債下跌，LQD下跌0.27%，HYG與JNK各下跌0.09%。企業融資的焦點則集中在大型投資計畫的後續發債需求，以及不同發行人能取得的條件。

## 加拿大通膨加速，歐洲短天期利率卻回落

加拿大5月消費者物價年增3.2%，高於前期2.8%；月增1.0%，季節調整後為0.5%。汽油價格年增33.2%，但排除汽油後的物價漲幅也從2.0%升至2.2%。食品上漲3.8%、運輸9.0%、服務2.0%。漲價範圍不只限於燃料，若趨勢延續，加拿大央行的觀望空間將縮小。

歐洲方面，ECB總裁拉加德表示，長期通膨預期仍大致穩定，因此中東衝擊目前尚不要求更強烈的政策回應。她發言後，交易員對年底前升息的定價由37降至33個基點，德國2年期公債殖利率下跌6個基點至2.59%。不過，歐元區核心通膨已由2.2%升至2.6%，市場仍預期存款利率至少再升1碼至2.5%。Jose Luis Escrivá提醒，能源成本已反映於運輸服務，工資傳導則尚未獲得證實。歐盟執委會信心指標在歐元區改善至−17.7、全歐盟改善至−17.0，但仍偏弱。

在假日前已承受政治壓力的英國首相Keir Starmer辭職。10年期英國公債殖利率下降4個基點至4.80%，英鎊對美元及歐元小幅走強；市場受到現行支出與債務限制可能維持的說法安撫。Wes Streeting被認為較可能保留Rachel Reeves的財政規則，Ed Miliband則較能容忍增加借款；Yvette Cooper與John Healey也被討論，但沒有確立的經濟政策。Streeting表態支持Andy Burnham後，英債與英鎊進一步走強，漫長黨魁爭奪的可能性下降。不過，最終領導人與財政大臣人選，仍將決定規則是否改變。

日本的政策與債券買盤也在變化。首相高市早苗雖長期傾向寬鬆，仍接受日本央行最近一次升息；副總裁Ryozo Himino則警告，不能拖延處理輸入性通膨。5月全國通膨維持1.4%，部分受能源補貼壓低。保險公司5月淨賣出¥2,012億剩餘天期逾10年的政府債，當時殖利率升至多年高點；退休基金相關機構的買進則創近2年最多。30年期殖利率約3.9%，仍低於一位策略師認為可能引發更多保險公司賣壓的4.5%水準。國內買家對較高殖利率的反應並不一致。

中國維持1年期LPR 3.00%及5年期以上LPR 3.50%，主要銀行貸款與房貸參考利率未變。韓國第1季實質GDP成長3.8%，實質國內總所得卻成長13.2%，反映晶片價格上漲，使購買力增幅遠高於產出。總統政策顧問警告，過剩資金可能流入房地產；韓國央行維持2.5%，但立場轉向偏鷹。出口帶來的收益，尚未解決國內信用與房市問題。

## 哥倫比亞選後上漲，巴西干預匯市並取消標售

巴西央行在成長加速、通膨高於目標與財政刺激仍存的情況下降息，財政部隨後取消原訂的NTN-B通膨連動債標售。2029年5月到期債券殖利率本月已上升逾80個基點至8.81%。政府另賣出即期美元、同時減少部分外匯交換部位，意在防止本地美元利率進一步上升。交換期貨利率回落，雷亞爾小幅走強，表現優於多數同業。這些操作緩解眼前賣壓，沒有消除財政與通膨方面的爭議。

墨西哥推介新2037年期債券及續發2056年期券，擬用所得買回2027、2028年到期美元債，以及2029年到期歐元債。S&P已將展望轉為負面，穆迪則因財政弱勢、債務增加與支援Pemex，把主權評級降至投資級最低一檔。墨西哥去年發債$410億，許多與支援Pemex有關；今年1月另發行$90億美元債及€95億歐元債。替換近期到期債務有助管理時程，最終定價才會顯示延長天期的成本。主權與Pemex雖有財務連結，仍是不同借款人。

阿根廷授權向認可金融機構借入最高$50億美元貸款，部分由多邊機構擔保。下個月有近$45億債券款項到期，明年外幣債務償付預計超過$200億。獲准借款上限不等於已取得資金，貸款條件與保證架構，將決定實際能減輕多少再融資風險。

哥倫比亞總統選舉後，市場反應截然不同。美元債領漲新興市場，披索上漲逾1.2%，同時廣泛新興市場貨幣指數卻下跌；交換利率最多下降28個基點，2030年本地債殖利率下降35個基點至12.1%。投資人歡迎Abelardo de la Espriella勝選，以及政策更偏市場的可能。對本地殖利率可能再降150至200個基點的看法仍是預測，取決於未來施政與政策落實。

塞內加爾貿易部長表示，可以重新談判或重整債務。先前發現$70億未揭露借款後，IMF暫停$18億安排，國際債市仍對該國關閉。這項表態提高了債務處理的政治接受度，但尚未確定債權人待遇或恢復援助的條件。委內瑞拉主權債與PDVSA債則跌至2個月低點，投資人等待針對估計$1,500億至$2,000億債務的可持續性檢視；主權債報酬自5月中旬下跌約6%。兩國債權回收價值仍充滿不確定性。

美元指數上升，廣泛新興市場貨幣指標下跌0.25%，波蘭茲羅提、菲律賓披索與匈牙利福林跌幅居前；EMB下跌0.34%。哥倫比亞上漲、巴西干預的反差，顯示美國實質殖利率走高時，各國仍有很不一樣的結果。

## SpaceX股價大跌，晶片股仍上漲

S&P 500下跌0.37%，Nasdaq 100下跌0.19%，費城半導體指數卻上漲2.04%，VIX則上升5.37%至17.28。SpaceX股價下跌16%，拖累大盤；當可流通股份不多、資金需求預期又龐大，股價波動可能格外劇烈。晶片硬體仍得到買盤。

談判代表表示美伊最終協議取得重大進展，WTI因此下跌2.32%至$74.82，布蘭特下跌2.44%至$77.90；兩者一週跌幅分別為7.34%與6.34%。較低油價使美債通膨補償下降，名目與實質殖利率仍因政策預期而上升。

美元指數小漲0.17%至101.02，黃金下跌1.00%至$4,181.90。實質殖利率與美元上升、油價下降，減輕一項通膨來源的同時，也提高美元借款成本。半導體股逆勢上漲，顯示股市並非全面拋售。

## 數據與債券供給將檢驗假日後的賣壓

6月23日將公布採購經理人初值。美國25日集中發布PCE通膨、個人所得與支出、耐久財訂單、第1季GDP終值及初領失業救濟金人數。這些數據將顯示，在原油走低之際，服務與核心物價是否仍支持Goolsbee的通膨疑慮。

財政部6月23日標售$690億2年期公債，24日$700億5年期，25日$440億7年期；同時還有國庫券、浮動利率券續發及公債買回。SpaceX與Sony也在推介美元債，截至週一報告時均未完成定價。標售需求、交易商承接，以及新公司債最終必須給出的利差，將顯示投資人能否在較高實質殖利率下吸收更大的發行量。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Treasuries Fall as Real Yields Rise Despite Cheaper Oil

Treasuries sold off when US bond markets reopened Monday, even as progress toward a lasting US-Iran agreement pulled oil lower. The 2-year yield rose 5 basis points to 4.24% and the 10-year gained 5 to 4.51%; the 5-year climbed 6 to 4.29% and the 30-year added 5 to 4.95%. The 10-year real yield rose more than the nominal yield, while inflation compensation declined. Investors were paying for a higher real-rate path under the Federal Reserve, not a larger long-term oil premium.

Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said services inflation was moving in the wrong direction, a concern he did not attribute simply to tariffs or the Iran-related energy shock. A New York Fed research model also raised its estimates for inflation, growth and the equilibrium real rate. The comments landed after Kevin Warsh's first meeting, when officials projected higher inflation and traders moved toward an October rate increase. Oil relief was no longer enough to bring Treasury yields down on its own.

The day's financing news sharpened that contrast. SpaceX began investor calls for a debut investment-grade bond sale of at least $20 billion while its shares fell 16%. Sony also returned to the dollar market, and two large bill auctions found buyers, showing continued access to capital even as its price rose. In Britain, a change of prime minister brought gilts some relief; in Canada, broader inflation raised the opposite policy concern. Across emerging markets, Colombia's election lifted bonds and its currency, while Brazil canceled an inflation-linked auction and intervened in foreign exchange.

## Policy Risk Pushes Up Real Yields

The 2s10s Treasury spread held at 27 basis points and the 2s30s at 71 as yields rose almost in parallel. Both curves remained much flatter than a week earlier, by 13 and 19 basis points respectively. The 5-year lagged its neighbors slightly, lifting the 2s5s10s butterfly 2 basis points to -17; 2s10s30s was unchanged at -17. Monday was a fresh decline in bond prices, not a renewed long-end steepening.

Five-year real yields rose 5 basis points to 2.01%, 7-year yields gained 6 to 2.13%, and the 10-year added 7 to 2.28%. At longer maturities, 20-year real yields rose 6 to 2.58% and the 30-year increased 5 to 2.75%. Ten-year breakeven inflation fell 2 basis points to 2.23%, more than offset by the real-yield rise. That divergence extended the Fed-driven shift already visible before the Juneteenth closure.

Goolsbee called services inflation particularly troubling because it could not be readily explained by the temporary energy or tariff effects. He also expressed openness to less forward guidance, consistent with Warsh's desire to make policy more responsive to incoming data. The New York Fed's June DSGE research model raised its 2026 core PCE forecast to 3.1% from 2.5% in March, GDP growth to 1.2% from 1.0%, and its estimate of the fourth-quarter natural real rate to 2.0% from 1.9%. Those are staff model outputs rather than official policy forecasts, but the simultaneous revisions gave investors a concrete account of why real yields might remain high.

Cash rates showed the distinction between the current funding market and expected future policy. Four- and 6-week bill yields eased 3 and 1 basis points to 3.63% and 3.65%, while the 13-week closed at 3.79% and the 52-week at 4.03%. The steeper rise farther along the bill curve was consistent with expected Fed restraint, without a common jump in the shortest cash maturities.

Treasury's $89 billion 91-day sale stopped at a 3.695% high discount rate, or 3.782% on an investment-rate basis, with 2.68 bid-to-cover. Of $87.168 billion in competitive awards, indirect bidders received $52.087 billion, direct bidders $4.238 billion and dealers $30.843 billion. The $77 billion 182-day issue stopped at 3.840% discount, or 3.970% investment rate, with 2.51 cover and 97.87% of bids at the high rate allotted. Indirect, direct and dealer awards were $40.073 billion, $3.000 billion and $32.481 billion of $75.553 billion in competitive bids accepted. Both issues settle June 25. The auctions showed substantial participation; settlement will bring a separate cash demand later in the week.

## SpaceX Shares Slide as Its First Bond Sale Takes Shape

SpaceX began calls for its first investment-grade dollar bonds, targeting at least $20 billion across maturities from 5 to 30 years. Proceeds are intended to refinance a bridge loan of roughly the same size, most of its $29.1 billion in long-term debt. Moody's assigned Baa1, Fitch BBB+ and S&P BBB; the company reported almost $101 billion in cash and equivalents as of June 19. Investors had not yet priced the bonds or built a final order book.

Its shares fell 16% to $154.60, bringing the three-session loss to 23% and wiping out more than $600 billion of market value. The stock remained about 15% above the $135 IPO price, and only 4.2% of shares had been available for trading on the first day. The small float amplified volatility, while the prospective bond sale put attention on the cash needs of a capital-intensive investment program. One analyst projection placed SpaceX net debt above $400 billion by 2031, from around $13 billion recently. That figure is a forecast, not the current balance sheet.

High-grade issuance had topped $120 billion by mid-June, a first-half sales pace three standard deviations above normal. The 15 biggest transactions accounted for about 57%, including Nvidia's roughly $25 billion sale. Credit spreads had changed little across the wave, but concentration in a few technology borrowers means further supply will test whether investors keep granting the same terms. Technology issuers have raised more than $300 billion of AI-linked debt across credit markets since November; Nvidia's earlier orders exceeded three times its deal size.

Sony added a Japanese high-grade borrower to the calendar. It began calls for 5- and 10-year dollar notes for general corporate purposes, its first return to the US dollar market since a $1.5 billion issue in 1998. Expected ratings were A2 and A+. Denso's $500 million dollar note, Mitsubishi's $1 billion sale and Toyota's €1 billion transaction also reflected Japanese issuers diversifying funding as domestic rates rose.

Robinhood pursued a different source of low-coupon financing. It marketed $2 billion of zero-coupon convertibles due in 2029, with a 60%-65% conversion premium. About $300 million was earmarked for share repurchases, and a derivative overlay was intended to offset dilution up to 125% of the reference share price. Pricing was scheduled after the New York close; the terms available during the session were still proposed, rather than an executed sale.

India's securitization market offered another route for lenders. Asset-backed issuance reached 1.53 trillion rupees in the year ended March; foreign banks' share rose to about 35% from 28%-30% in each of the previous two fiscal years. Retail-loan pools can meet priority-sector requirements with different regulatory capital treatment from some direct loans. Aye Finance said securitized funding cost it 75-100 basis points less than a local bond because its pools were rated 3-4 notches above the company's own rating. Those savings depend on performance of the underlying retail, vehicle, personal and gold loans.

More fragile borrowers faced negotiations about debt structure, not merely yield. Godiva Japan sought a nine-month extension on about ¥75 billion, or $464 million, due at month-end from 25 banks. Mitsubishi UFJ was considering ¥5 billion of new money senior to existing debt if the company defaulted. Godiva lost around ¥30 billion in 2025, and its equity ratio had fallen to roughly 7%, against about 40% or more at typical Japanese companies. An extension would buy time but could change existing creditors' priority.

Deutsche Bank analysts valued Paragon's €450 million 2030 secured bond at 70-75 cents on the euro, against a market quote near 83, citing acquisition-led leverage and integration risk. The company pointed to strong customer retention, only about 27% of net revenue from its top 10 clients, and no major maturity before 2030. The dispute concerned future credit quality rather than an imminent payment failure. A UK consolidated bond tape covering more than 95% of bonds traded across venues also went live, improving visibility into secondary prices as supply expands.

California may add public borrowing to the calendar. Lawmakers agreed to put an $11.3 billion housing package on the November ballot, including $10 billion of general-obligation bonds and $1.25 billion of self-supporting revenue bonds for veterans' home loans. A separate $12 billion science and health proposal was still being considered. None of these bonds had been approved by voters or issued. The measures respond to a median single-family home price above $900,000, but would add public duration if authorized.

Listed credit funds softened with the Treasury selloff: LQD fell 0.27%, HYG 0.09% and JNK 0.09%. Their small moves sat beside the much larger questions of who can issue, under what terms, and how much more debt large investment programs will require.

## Canada's Inflation Rises as European Rates Ease

May Canadian consumer prices rose 3.2% from a year earlier, up from 2.8%, and increased 1.0% on the month, or 0.5% seasonally adjusted. Gasoline inflation reached 33.2%, but prices excluding gasoline also accelerated to 2.2% from 2.0%. Food rose 3.8%, transport 9.0% and services 2.0%. The increase was broader than fuel alone, limiting the Bank of Canada's room to wait if the trend persists.

In Europe, ECB President Christine Lagarde said the Middle East shock did not yet require a stronger response because long-term inflation expectations remained broadly anchored. Traders reduced the year-end tightening priced into swaps to 33 basis points from 37, and Germany's 2-year yield fell 6 basis points to 2.59%. Euro-area core inflation had nevertheless risen to 2.6% from 2.2%, and markets still expected at least another quarter-point increase to a 2.5% deposit rate. Jose Luis Escrivá warned that energy costs had reached transport services while wage effects remained unproven. The Commission's confidence gauges improved to -17.7 in the euro area and -17.0 in the EU, but both remained weak.

UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer resigned after the political pressure described before the holiday. Ten-year gilt yields fell 4 basis points to 4.80% and sterling edged higher against the dollar and euro, as investors were reassured that current spending and debt constraints could remain. Wes Streeting was regarded as more likely to keep Rachel Reeves's fiscal rules, while Ed Miliband was associated with greater borrowing tolerance; Yvette Cooper and John Healey were also discussed without settled economic platforms. Gilts and sterling strengthened after Streeting backed Andy Burnham, reducing the prospect of a prolonged contest. The choice of leader and chancellor still mattered for any future change to the rules.

Japan's policy and buyer base continued to change. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi accepted the BOJ's latest increase despite her preference for accommodation, while Deputy Governor Ryozo Himino warned against delaying action on imported inflation. Nationwide May inflation held at 1.4%, partly because of energy subsidies. Insurers sold a net ¥201.2 billion of government bonds with more than 10 years to maturity in May as yields reached multidecade highs, while pension-fund proxies made their largest purchases in almost two years. The 30-year yield near 3.9% was below a strategist's 4.5% level associated with greater insurer selling. Different domestic buyers were responding differently to higher yields.

China held its one-year loan prime rate at 3.00% and its over-five-year benchmark at 3.50%, leaving key bank-loan and mortgage references unchanged. South Korean first-quarter real GDP grew 3.8%, while real gross domestic income rose 13.2% as higher chip prices lifted purchasing power faster than output. A presidential policy adviser warned that excess liquidity could flow into property; the Bank of Korea had held at 2.5% with a more hawkish bias. The export windfall had not, by itself, settled the domestic credit and housing question.

## Colombia Rallies; Brazil Intervenes and Cancels Supply

Brazil's Treasury canceled a planned NTN-B inflation-linked bond auction after a central-bank rate cut amid faster growth, above-target inflation and fiscal stimulus. Yields on inflation-linked bonds due May 2029 had risen more than 80 basis points during the month to 8.81%. The government also sold spot dollars while reducing part of its FX-swap position, seeking to prevent local dollar rates from rising further. Swap futures declined and the real firmed slightly, outperforming most peers. The operations eased immediate market pressure without resolving the underlying fiscal or inflation dispute.

Mexico marketed new 2037 bonds and a reopening of 2056 notes to fund repurchases of dollar debt due in 2027 and 2028 and euro debt due in 2029. S&P had moved its outlook to negative; Moody's had lowered the sovereign rating to the bottom investment-grade tier, citing fiscal weakness, rising debt and Pemex support. Mexico sold $41 billion of debt last year, much of it tied to that support, and issued $9 billion in dollars and €9.5 billion in January. Replacing near maturities can help manage the calendar; final pricing will determine the cost. The sovereign and Pemex remain separate borrowers.

Argentina authorized up to $5 billion of dollar loans from recognized financial institutions, partially backed by multilaterals. Nearly $4.5 billion of bond payments fall due next month, and foreign-currency debt service is expected to exceed $20 billion next year. The authorized ceiling is not completed borrowing; lenders' terms and the guarantee structure will determine how much rollover risk is displaced.

Colombia supplied a very different market reaction after its presidential vote. Dollar bonds led emerging-market gains, the peso rose more than 1.2% as a wider developing-currency gauge fell, and swap rates dropped as much as 28 basis points. The 2030 local-bond yield fell 35 basis points to 12.1%. Investors welcomed Abelardo de la Espriella's victory and prospects for a more market-oriented government. Forecasts for another 150-200 basis points of local-yield declines remain expectations, contingent on governing and policy delivery.

Senegal's trade minister said debt could be renegotiated or restructured after $7 billion of previously unreported borrowing led the IMF to suspend a $1.8 billion program. International bond access remains closed. The statement showed greater acceptance of a debt operation, without settling creditor treatment or the conditions for renewed support. Venezuelan sovereign and PDVSA bonds fell to two-month lows ahead of a debt-sustainability review for an estimated $150-$200 billion of obligations; sovereign returns had declined about 6% since mid-May. Recovery values remained uncertain in both cases.

The dollar index rose and a developing-currency gauge slipped 0.25%, with the Polish zloty, Philippine peso and Hungarian forint among the weakest. EMB fell 0.34%. Those broad moves contrasted with Colombia's rally and Brazil's intervention, showing how much local outcomes diverged as US real yields rose.

## SpaceX Stock Drops While Chip Shares Rise

The S&P 500 fell 0.37% and the Nasdaq 100 lost 0.19%, but the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rose 2.04%. VIX climbed 5.37% to 17.28. SpaceX's 16% share-price drop weighed on the broader market and highlighted the volatility possible when a small free float meets large funding expectations; chip hardware still attracted buyers.

WTI fell 2.32% to $74.82 and Brent dropped 2.44% to $77.90 as negotiators reported progress toward a final US-Iran agreement. Their weekly declines were 7.34% and 6.34%. The lower oil prices helped push Treasury inflation compensation down, but nominal and real yields rose as policy expectations prevailed.

The dollar index edged up 0.17% to 101.02 and gold fell 1.00% to $4,181.90. The combination of higher real yields, a stronger dollar and lower oil offered relief from one inflation source while increasing the cost of borrowing in dollars. It did not produce a uniform equity selloff, as the semiconductor gain showed.

## Data and Supply Will Test the Post-Holiday Selloff

Flash purchasing-manager surveys arrive June 23. The US June 25 release block includes PCE inflation, personal income and spending, durable-goods orders, a final first-quarter GDP estimate and initial claims. The results will show whether services and core-price strength support Goolsbee's concern even as crude falls.

Treasury sells $69 billion of 2-year notes June 23, $70 billion of 5-year notes June 24 and $44 billion of 7-year notes June 25, alongside bills, a floating-rate reopening and buybacks. SpaceX and Sony are also marketing dollar bonds; neither had completed pricing in Monday's report. Auction demand, dealer awards and the eventual concessions on new corporate debt will show how easily investors absorb the larger calendar at higher real yields.

Australia's May CPI, a BOJ summary of opinions, Bank of Canada deliberations and the EIA petroleum report are due June 24; an ECB bulletin follows June 25. The details will show whether energy relief is reaching underlying prices abroad. Brazil's inflation-linked yields and dollar funding, Mexico's final liability-management terms and Argentina's guaranteed-loan structure remain the more specific sovereign financing tests.
